dedupe_keys.name: us first end to end space weather tabletop exercise 8 to 9 may 2024 after action report

description: This case study is the after-action report of the first end-to-end United States tabletop exercise for a severe space weather event, held on 8 and 9 May 2024. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration, NOAA's satellite data service, the National Science Foundation and the Federal Emergency Management Agency sponsored it, and the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory hosted and reported it. Participants from more than thirty government bodies played four modules of a scenario with satellite radiation damage, radio outages, degraded GPS, lost satellite tracking and regional power outages, following the Homeland Security exercise programme method, while the real Gannon Storm began the same day. Coverage is national, with two sites. The findings call for clearer impact-based notifications, a whole-of-government approach and better forecasting. Format and access: a 208-page PDF report and a NESDIS news story, free to read; the pages read state no licence. Caveats: it is a discussion exercise, not a measured response, and only the first 12 pages were read. It supports resilience planning for emergency response to solar storms. Related catalogue records are the NOAA satellite environment testbed exercise 2023 and the 2024 solar maximum mitigation review.

name: US first end-to-end Space Weather Tabletop Exercise, 8 to 9 May 2024: after-action report
outcomes: The exercise showed the need for better coordinated space weather notifications that state impacts on critical infrastructure and for whole-of-government planning; 93 percent of participants agreed it enhanced cross-agency communication and all agreed it generated important dialogue. Gaps in forecasting and public messaging were recorded.
